title: Why Tough drank: dipsomania versus musicians' lives
summary: Dance asks what drove Tough to drink; Freeman says musicians don't drink because they are musicians, and Tough and Bix were dipsomaniacs.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I am just wondering what accounted for Davey's compulsion to drink. I mean, he had a terrific joie de vivre, he had a greater appreciation of life than most anybody of his contemporaries, I should think. Whether it was -- he surely should not have suffered from a sense of inadequacy since he was tremendously talented. What do you think drove Davey to that?
Well, with all due respect to your question about the drinking, don't you think, Helen, that it doesn't really matter much what a person is, men don't drink because they are musicians.

There are hundreds of thousands of people around the world of whom we shall never hear, who are drunkards and addicts. We will not hear of them because they are not in the limelight, so that all people in the arts who become famous are considered to be either addicts or drunkards, which isn't true, really. If you look --Dave Tough and Bix just happened
to be dipsomaniacs. Now a dipsomaniac differs from a drunkard, doesn't he?
